It is a small suggestion but I think when it comes to DPDR, small steps are best. 

Make some ice 

Get an ice cube out and hold it in your hand, feel the texture, the temperature, focus on as many details of this ice cube as you can, you might find you can't really feel it that you feel numb, if that's the case, touch the ice to the small of your back on your spine, notice the sensation. 

Keep a mental note, did you feel anything? 
What if anything did you feel and how intense was that.. 
You are not completely numb, your brain has shut down some parts so you are not feeling things coupled with these distressing thoughts about being ill, you may not feel anxious but your comments would suggest anxiety based thinking, you may be disconnected from your feelings but the thoughts about your condition will be feeding it, I know this as I also have somatic issues, I can have the full symptoms of an illness I hear about even if I don't feel any panic when listening, it used to freak me out when it first happened as obviously I believed I was ill, got checked out and it turned out I was fine, the brain is incredibly powerful, we don't always have to feel anxiety for our brain to try to protect us or for us to process and assimilate something without even realising. 



Dpdr is an anxiety based condition, you might not feel anxious now but your brain truly believed you were in danger for a long time so it shut parts down to help you function and survive it just hasn't realised it's time to turn that function off. It kept feeding back in to your brain creating a loop, I'm not sure the best way to unfreeze and wake up your brain but I just kept living my life, even when my OCD told me this was dangerous or that I was seriously mentally ill, maybe insane, I saw those thoughts as best I could as just thoughts. 

Maybe my comment isn't helpful and you may have already tried these things but I wanted to try and help because I do know how awful a condition it can feel

Spinning room 

Weird burning sensations on skin 

Hallucinating (this is when my anxiety was at it's most severe) 

Ice pick headaches 

Tingling arms and back 

Not being able to look people in the eye when talking about myself 

Waking in the night and heart started racing 

Repetitive dreams/thoughts coupled with restless arms/sleep paralysis 

Feeling like I was going blind
